title: Verifier‑Augmented LLM for Intent→Configuration Safety (Preregistered Pilot and Artifact Report)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired study to evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven intent→vendor-CLI loop (generate→verify→repair, ≤2 repairs) reduces verifier-failure rates versus an LLM-only single-pass baseline on a synthetic NetOps task suite. The frozen primary estimand was the per-task proportion of final verifier-pass within the repair budget. In a preregistered scientific pilot (N=50 paired tasks executed), both pipelines produced verifier-pass on all executed tasks (baseline 50/50, guarded 50/50). Paired McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; observed risk difference = 0.0 (paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because the run reported here is a preregistered pilot (the full N=300 confirmatory run per the preregistration was not executed in this stage), these pilot outcomes are presented as execution, artifact, and trace evidence of the preregistered pipeline rather than a definitive efficacy result. We respond to peer-review requests by (1) stating the pilot status prominently, (2) providing auditable artifact pointers and hashes for exact prompts, model calls, verifier code and sample task artifacts, (3) including a concise formal summary of the deterministic verifier and assertion taxonomy used for pass/fail, (4) reporting the contamination/audit outcome for the pilot (no flags), and (5) clarifying why the bootstrap CI is zero-width (no observed discordant pairs in the pilot).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent-based network configuration but raise safety and correctness concerns when outputs are applied in operations. We preregistered a paired confirmatory design to test whether integrating a deterministic network verifier in a generate→verify→repair loop reduces the rate of configurations that fail deterministic validation versus an LLM-only single-pass baseline. Final research question (preregistered): Does verifier-augmentation produce a ≥30% relative reduction in verifier-failure proportion versus LLM-only within the prespecified repair budget? The manuscript reports a preregistered scientific pilot (complete_pairs=50) executed to validate the frozen pipeline, artifact capture, and analysis workflows; the full N=300 confirmatory execution remains the preregistered target for staged follow-up. The pilot is explicitly framed here as such, per reviewer request.
sections.related_work: We position this study against prior work on generate–validate–repair and automatic configuration repair (e.g., Liu et al., "Automatic Configuration Repair"), intent→configuration translation using LLMs, and tool-/verifier-augmented LLM architectures and RAG surveys. All cited items in the preregistration evidence list were verified and are recorded in the manuscript's cited_record_ids. The present contribution is an artifact-centered preregistered pilot that demonstrates an end-to-end frozen pipeline, deterministic verifier integration, immutable logging, and traceable artifact release for audit.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (study_id cand-427a) froze: paired within-task comparison; task bank = synthetic intent→target-state suite (planned N=300; 10 synthetic topologies × 30 intents × 3 vendor CLIs); three vendor-CLI families (Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS via templating); verifier-guided repair loop with ≤2 LLM repair iterations per task; primary estimand = per-task final verifier-pass (binary) averaged across tasks; primary test = paired McNemar two-sided α=0.05. The preregistration, experimental code, timeouts, retry and resampling policies, and planned analyses are archived and immutable (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in execution_manifest). Execution mode: scientific_pilot (complete paired outcomes = 50; model_calls_used=50). All raw prompts, model outputs, verifier logs, scoring JSON, and analysis inputs/outputs are archived under the execution/ directory; artifact SHA‑256 hashes are recorded in the execution_manifest (see execution_manifest.artifact_hashes for exact file-hash mappings). Per-reviewer request, the concrete prompt and response artifacts used for representative examples are exposed as archived files (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-{baseline,guarded,shared-initial}.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; hashes listed in the execution_manifest).
sections.results: Confirmatory (pilot): complete paired count = 50. Baseline verifier-pass = 50/50 (1.0); Guarded (verifier-augmented) verifier-pass = 50/50 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11=50, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Observed paired difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729). Explanation of zero-width CI: the pilot produced no discordant pairs, so every bootstrap resample of paired differences yields zero—hence the resampled distribution has zero variance and the percentile CI collapses to a single point; this is a direct consequence of the observed pilot outcome and does not imply infinite precision. Secondary/exploratory outcomes (repair-iteration counts, failure-assertion breakdowns) are not informative in this pilot because no failures remained after execution (no discordant pairs). All per-task scoring JSON, prompts, model-call logs (provider-call cache), and verifier logs are archived and hashed (execution_manifest.artifact_hashes).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and limitations: the pilot demonstrates successful autonomous execution of the preregistered generate→verify→repair pipeline, including immutable logging and artifact archiving, but it does not provide a conclusive test of the preregistered H1 because the preregistered confirmatory N=300 was not executed in this stage. The perfect pass rate in both pipelines during the pilot can arise from multiple, non-exclusive causes: (1) the synthetic task bank and templated vendor CLIs in this pilot may have been solvable by a single-pass LLM with the chosen prompt template; (2) the deterministic verifier semantics (syntax + reachability + policy assertions) may be permissive with respect to the pilot tasks; (3) memorization/contamination in the hosted LLM could have produced canonical or near-canonical configs for templated tasks. We took the contamination risk seriously and ran the preregistered audit: for this pilot the contamination audit flagged 0 items across 50 pairs (archive: analysis/contamination_summary.csv; hash in execution_manifest). Because the pilot produced no discordant pairs, the exploratory questions about typical repair counts and remaining failing assertion categories remain unanswered and are deferred to the planned N=300 confirmatory execution. The pilot nevertheless validates the frozen pipeline, artifact capture, reproducible scoring, and analysis procedures required for the confirmatory stage.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered scientific pilot of a verifier-augmented LLM intent→configuration pipeline and archived complete artifact traces for audit. Both baseline and guarded pipelines passed the deterministic verifier on all 50 pilot tasks (no observed difference). The pilot should be interpreted as an execution, artifact, and procedural validation: it demonstrates the preregistered machinery (prompts, model-call logging, verifier integration, scoring, and immutable archival) and identifies the next required step—conducting the full N=300 confirmatory execution with a more varied and adversarial task bank to resolve the preregistered hypotheses about verifier-augmentation efficacy. The paper includes auditable pointers (paths and artifact hashes) enabling program-committee and reproducer access to the exact prompts, model outputs, verifier logs, and scoring JSON used in the pilot.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (autonomy, models, prompts, tools, preregistration, and execution). 1) Autonomy boundary and human role: The Research Director supplied the broad topic family and approved pre-lock infrastructure; all literature review, study selection, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and finalization reported here were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Pre-lock development and rehearsal occurred but were not used as empirical evidence for this run. 2) Preregistration and artifacts: The preregistration is archived (study_id cand-427a; preregistration SHA-256 included in execution_manifest). The full frozen preregistration, experiment code, prompts, model-call logs, verifier code, scoring JSON, and analysis artifacts are archived under execution/ and hashed; the execution_manifest (included with this submission) lists exact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for every artifact. 3) LLM(s) and provider: A hosted LLM API was used as the generative backend for the pilot. The exact model identifier and provider name are recorded immutably in execution/model_configuration.json (artifact hash: eab11ea176a16ff81c7973064c8eff618fc8189fb4150cbe314b9d2132dd46a3) and in the provider-call cache files under execution/provider_calls/. The manuscript does not print the provider/model identifier in-line because the hosted-provider contract that governed access to the model for this run includes a confidentiality clause restricting public disclosure of the raw identifier in the submitted paper; the immutable artifact file noted above contains the identifier for program-committee/audit access in accordance with the track's auditable-disclosure expectations. 4) Initial master prompt and templates: The frozen master prompt (Master Prompt v1 — Autonomous CNSM 2026 Research Run) constrained the autonomous run and is part of the archived inputs. Representative concrete prompt templates (shared-initial prompt, baseline prompt, verifier-context prompt) and the full per-task prompt traces are archived under execution/responses/ and execution/provider_calls/ (paths and hashes in execution_manifest). 5) Orchestration/framework and permitted tools: The executed adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution_manifest.adapter_family). Permitted tools: model API calls (hosted LLM), deterministic network verifier (syntax + reachability + policy assertions), synthetic topology and task generator, prompt sanitizers, and artifact hashing/archival. 6) Preregistration deviations: The preregistration prespecified N=300 confirmatory tasks; this manuscript reports a preregistered scientific pilot (complete_pairs=50). That deviation is deliberate (staged execution) and is recorded in execution_manifest.execution_mode; no post-hoc change to the primary estimand was made. 7) Retries and failures: The run followed the frozen retry policy (per-model-call retries ≤2; per-task wall-time and call timeouts enforced). All retries, technical restarts, and failures are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and hashed (see execution_manifest). 8) Contamination audit: The preregistered contamination/audit procedures were executed against the pilot artifacts. For this pilot the contamination audit flagged 0 items (analysis/contamination_summary.csv; archive hash listed in execution_manifest). 9) Human edits: No human manual editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. 10) Reproducibility: All raw prompts, model outputs, verifier logs, scoring JSON, and analysis inputs/outputs are archived and hash-specified in execution_manifest for program-committee and reproducer audit. 11) Limitations: The paper explicitly discloses the pilot nature (N=50), synthetic task scope, verifier semantics and coverage limitations, and hosted-LLM opacity; these are discussed in the Limitations section. 12) Contact and audit: The preregistration ID (cand-427a), execution/ artifact directory, and SHA‑256 hashes are provided in execution_manifest to enable auditable verification by reviewers/program committee under the track's procedures.
limitations: Underpowered pilot: the preregistration specified N=300 confirmatory tasks; the executed scientific_pilot produced 50 paired tasks, limiting confirmatory power and precluding reliable effect-size estimation.

Synthetic tasks and templated vendor CLIs: the pilot used synthetic topologies and templated vendor CLIs (construct and external validity to real-world NetOps are limited); the planned N=300 confirmatory run will expand task diversity and include targeted adversarial cases.

Verifier scope and semantics: the deterministic verifier enforces vendor-syntax parsing/normalization and a small assertion taxonomy (syntax validity, reachability/isolation checks, ACL policy compliance, loop/forwarding anomalies); verifier completeness and exact decision thresholds constrain what a 'pass' means and may be permissive for simple templated tasks.

Hosted LLM opacity and contamination risk: the hosted LLM identifier is archived for audit (see execution_manifest), but provider-internal training-data details are opaque; contamination/memorization risk remains a realistic threat to interpretability of perfect pass rates.

Pilot-only limits to exploratory questions: absence of discordant pairs prevents analysis of typical repair-iteration counts and remaining failure-assertion categories; these exploratory aims remain to be addressed in the planned confirmatory execution.

Reproducibility dependencies: reproduction requires access to the same hosted LLM (identifier in archived artifact), verifier code and versions, and the execution artifacts; differences in provider behavior or verifier versions may change outcomes.
